about.title: About
about.intro: Language is much more than vocabulary and grammar.

paragraphs.1: It is the way a child discovers the world, builds relationships, and develops a sense of belonging. Through language, families pass on stories, memories, values, and culture. That is why preserving a heritage language in a multilingual environment is about much more than learning another language—it is an investment in a child's connection to their family, their heritage, and their community.
paragraphs.2: This belief is what inspired Kutak za srpski.
paragraphs.3: We are a Serbian heritage language school for children growing up in New York and their families. Our programs are designed specifically for children acquiring Serbian as a heritage language and are grounded in current research in linguistics, psycholinguistics, developmental psychology, and language teaching methodology. Each program follows children's natural developmental stages while addressing the unique realities of growing up in a multilingual environment.
paragraphs.4: Language is acquired best when it is part of everyday life. That is why children learn through conversation, play, literature, music, movement, and shared exploration. Our goal is not for children to memorize vocabulary or grammar rules, but to use Serbian naturally, confidently, and with genuine understanding.
paragraphs.5: Parents are an equally important part of our work. Families play a central role in maintaining a heritage language, which is why we view our programs as a partnership with parents. We provide guidance, practical support, and an understanding of the unique challenges of raising children between two or more languages.
paragraphs.6: At Kutak, children develop much more than language skills. They build confidence, curiosity, and a sense of belonging. They learn to talk with their grandparents without translating, to understand the stories that shaped their families, and to read, sing, ask questions, imagine, and express themselves in the language that is part of who they are.
paragraphs.7: We do not measure success by the number of words a child has learned. We measure it by how naturally Serbian becomes part of your child's everyday life.
paragraphs.8: That is why Kutak is much more than a language school. It is a place where expertise meets warmth, where curiosity is nurtured, bilingualism is celebrated, and families preserve what they most hope to pass on to their children: the ability to understand one another, to connect, and to belong—in their own language.

founder.title: About the Founder
founder.bio: Kutak za srpski was founded by Ivana Đurović. She was born and raised in Belgrade, Serbia. She earned her bachelor's and master's degrees in English Language and Literature from the Faculty of Philology, University of Belgrade, followed by a master's degree in Linguistics from the University of Iowa. She also spent time in Brazil, where she taught English to students of different ages. While pursuing her doctoral studies in Linguistics at the CUNY Graduate Center in New York, Ivana welcomed her daughter, Klara. Becoming a mother inspired her to create the kind of community she wanted for her own child—a place where children growing up far from their parents' homeland could develop and preserve the Serbian language and the cultural heritage that comes with it. Throughout this journey, Ivana and Klara have been wholeheartedly supported by tata Michael.
founder.founding: **Kutak za srpski** was established in November 2025 as a series of workshops for the youngest learners, designed for children and families from New York and the surrounding area. From the very beginning, the idea was to create a place where children could listen, speak, and learn Serbian through play, stories, songs, and connection, while also discovering and nurturing the language and culture together with their families. This is the next step in building our shared center for Serbian language and culture—a space that will bring together children, parents, teachers, and the broader community, a place where the Serbian language has its natural home.

faqPage.title: FAQ
faqPage.intro: Frequently asked questions about our classes, enrollment, and language support.

1.q: Can we attend a trial class?
1.a: If spaces are still available after September 8, you will be welcome to attend one free trial class. We will announce available spots through our social media channels (Instagram and Facebook) and by email. If you are interested, please contact us by email.

2.q: What language levels are your programs designed for?
2.a:
For now, our programs are organized by age group rather than language proficiency level.

Our youngest program, Prve reci (First Words), for ages 1-3, is designed for children at all levels of Serbian language exposure and development.

For the older age groups (ages 3-5 and 5-7), children should have at least a basic understanding of Serbian. Depending on the child's speaking ability, there are two options:

- If a child can speak in Serbian sentences (even with some effort), they can attend classes independently.
- If a child understands Serbian but only uses a few words in Serbian, a parent or another adult family member should attend and actively participate in class.

3.q: My child does not know any Serbian at all. Will you offer classes for complete beginners?
3.a: If there is enough interest, we may organize beginner classes in the future. Until then, we encourage families to begin introducing Serbian into their child's everyday life at home. We will soon share practical tips on how to approach this challenging but important journey.

4.q: My child speaks Serbian fluently. What can Kutak offer our family?
4.a:
Congratulations! This is a wonderful achievement and the best possible foundation.

Unfortunately, a heritage language can be lost very quickly once children begin spending most of their day in preschool, school, or other environments where another language dominates. Kutak exists as a support against this natural shift.

Kutak is a place where children not only continue developing their Serbian skills, but also gain another reason to use Serbian: friendships, children's literature, play, and the community we are building together that strengthen all the efforts families already make to help their children stay connected to their language and cultural heritage.

5.q: My child is older than 7. Will you offer classes for older children?
5.a: If there is enough interest, we would be happy to organize a group for older children in the future. Reach out and tell your friends to reach out too.

6.q: I have two children in different age groups, but it is not practical to bring them to separate classes. Can I enroll them in the same group?
6.a: Yes, but please email us first so we can advise which group would be a better fit for both children.
